column3: NASB reads “Jesus Christ” in the order of other manuscripts; the critical text has “Christ Jesus.” It adds “our.”
NASB follows the critical text without “and the Lord Jesus Christ”; it reorders the verse. A full-width colon appears in the NASB text.
NASB follows the critical text without “and”; “continually” is rendered “always.”
NASB follows the critical text (“which you have”); it adds “since.”
NASB renders “heavens” as “heaven.”
NASB follows the critical text (“and increasing”); it adds “constantly” and “it has been doing,” and renders “knew” as “understood.”
NASB reads “on our behalf”; manuscripts differ between “our” and “your.”
NASB renders “having made known” as “informed.”
NASB reorders the verse, rendering “in all wisdom and spiritual understanding” as “in all spiritual wisdom and understanding.”
NASB follows the critical text; it renders “in all pleasing” as “to please Him in all respects.”
NASB adds “the attaining of” and renders “endurance” as “steadfastness” and “with joy” as “joyously.”
NASB reads “us,” following other manuscripts; the critical text has “you.” It renders “for the share of” as “to share in.”
NASB adds “For” and renders “dominion” as “domain.”
NASB follows the critical text without the Textus Receptus “through His blood.”
NASB renders “firstborn over all creation” as “the first-born of all creation.”
NASB follows the critical text; it renders “in Him” as “by Him” and “unto Him” as “for Him.”
NASB renders “have held together” as “hold together.”
NASB renders “holding preeminence” as “come to have first place.”
NASB supplies “the Father's” as the subject of “good pleasure”; the Greek leaves the subject unstated.
NASB adds “I say” and renders “heavens” as “heaven.”
NASB adds “although” and “engaged in.”
NASB renders “the body of His flesh” as “His fleshly body,” and “unblemished and blameless” as “blameless and beyond reproach.”
NASB follows the critical text; it renders “established and firm” as “firmly established and steadfast” and “have become” as “was made.”
NASB follows the critical text without “my”; it restructures the verse and puts “which is the church” in parentheses.
NASB adds “church” and renders “administration” as “stewardship” and “to complete the word” as “to fully carry out the preaching of the word.”
NASB follows the critical text; it adds “that is” and renders “ages” as “past ages.”
NASB follows the critical text (“what is,” “which is”).
NASB follows the critical text without “Jesus”; “perfect” is rendered “complete.”
NASB renders “energy” as “power” and “in power” as “mightily.”
